concepts.title: New Beginnings: Cities and States
concepts.definition: After the early second millennium BCE, new beginnings reshaped the subcontinent: iron tools cleared forests, villages multiplied, and people gathered into cities and states called janapadas and mahajanapadas.
concepts.key_idea: Better tools and growing surplus let villages grow into cities, and cities into states.

concepts.title: Kautilya's Ideal Kingdom
concepts.definition: Kautilya's Arthashastra describes a well-protected kingdom: a fortified capital, cultivable land, mines and forests, water not dependent on rain alone, good roads and a productive economy.
concepts.key_idea: A strong state plans for hard times: stores, forts and roads keep the people safe in calamities.

concepts.title: The Mahajanapadas and the Rise of Magadha
concepts.definition: Scores of mahajanapadas, each with a capital and an assembly, dotted the subcontinent; Magadha, with its fertile plains, iron and elephants, rose above them all and prepared the ground for empires.
concepts.key_idea: Location plus resources equals power: Magadha's rivers, iron and elephants made it first among states.

concepts.title: Life in the Cities and Villages
concepts.definition: New cities hummed with artisans, traders and officials, ringed by villages of farmers and herders who paid taxes; coins, weights and writing kept this growing economy moving.
concepts.key_idea: City and village fed each other: grain flowed in, goods, taxes and orders flowed out.
